limitations: The six aliases are exact source-profile mappings scoped to the pinned 2010 source file and sheet. This does not create a reusable generic region-name normalizer or prove that historical regional boundaries or legal statuses were stable. A shared named, typed historical GeoKLADR object supports settlement identity. It does not establish census-date administrative boundary stability, legal OKATO continuity, or population comparability.
Existing direct point origins are evidence of source-object continuity; this review admits no new coordinates, measurement date, provider/FIAS binding, or native code mapping.
Application relies on the pinned profile/stage raw row reopening and exact record locators; no full-source raw DBF or workbook reread was repeated here.
The fixed sample is targeted and non-probability; it supports scope review and is not a national error-rate estimate.
